answer: The registry erasure-codes a 2 TB corpus into a trellis of Reed-Solomon shards and assigns each newcomer a unique 64 GB slice, bound to its key by a Merkle root. Auditors then demand random 4 KB Merkle openings within 80 ms, which a node can meet only from local NVMe. Failures forfeit a 30-token bond per miss. Faking 10,000 identities needs 640 TB of flash, about $38,000 up front plus $2,100 monthly hosting, and 100 audits per hour would expose any pooled storage. A sybil operator hauling that much data resembles a hiker dragging a dune up a summit, every grain counted.
